bias: 'Friday's violent liquidation left sellers firmly in control, but critical structural references below and the potential for a ferocious cover rally make the next move anything but straightforward.' Friday was a violent trend day down that closed on downward spikes in both (ES 6954.25 → 6898, NQ 25199 → 24976.5). Both closed below their prior all-time highs and turned negative for the year. Weekly frame: 'Price has collapsed. Has value followed?' — the liquidation left very little volume behind it, so price moved but value has not been established lower; that is not a bottom and not yet a confirmed bear market. Not once since November 11 have RTH buyers initiated above a prior day's high; no credible swing low until they do and then break a multi-day balance to the upside. Friday's high is the upper boundary of any prospective balance. Trading lower first gives clarity: either a LBAF of Friday's low (possible ferocious cover rally) or a break with continuation (objective short). Opening and holding inside Friday's range is the murkiest case — and 'somehow therefore the most likely'.
wildcard: Short setups are 'objectively excellent' but a cover rally can push through strong levels; if the A-grade shorts consistently fail, that failure is itself a clue that a real cover rally is underway. All shorts get an immediate mental downgrade with an active LBAF of Friday's low, and a smaller one if buyers repeatedly defend the spike base. Trading inside the spike is 'objectively indeterminate', slight edge to sellers. 'For roughly 100 handles below Friday's low, the market can remain objectively short while carrying extreme risk that sellers get their faces ripped off.' Poor short location does not make a long setup. He takes no swing positions this shortened holiday week — day trades only. 'NQ could be up or down 5% on Monday and neither outcome would particularly surprise me.'
